question.text: A thin uniform rod of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, cross sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> is rotated about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to its length with angular velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi></math>. If value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi></math> in terms of its rotational kinetic energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mfrac></msqrt></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Rotational kinetic energy is given by E=12Iω2, here, I is moment of inertia of rod about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to it.

So, E=12ml212ω2

⇒E=12dAl312ω2    ∵mass=density×volume

⇒E=dA(2)324ω2

⇒ω=3EdA

Thus, the value of α=3.
